slice_results.behavior_summary: When executed (shell script), the code runs the Node.js executable with the script located at the same directory path as the batch file ("%~dp0\run") and passes all command-line arguments (%*), resulting in launching a Node.js process to execute the specified script.
slice_results.explanation: [LLM Judgment: Benign] The analyzed batch script simply runs a Node.js script located in the same directory, passing all command-line arguments. This behavior is common and legitimate for batch wrappers that launch Node.js applications. Unlike the known malicious patterns, which involve automatic execution during package installation hooks (preinstall/postinstall) and trigger further malicious actions such as data exfiltration or reverse shells, this script lacks any such context or additional suspicious operations. There is no evidence of obfuscation, automatic execution during install, or system manipulation beyond launching a Node.js process. The similarity to known malicious patterns is low and only superficial (running a Node.js script named 'run'), without the install-time automatic execution or malicious payload delivery.
